, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SURAJ GOVINDARAJ  and  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SURAJ GOVINDARAJ)
1.

The appellant is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
"Wherefore, the appellant most humbly prays that, the judgment and award dated 04/10/2017 in M.V.C.No.419/2013 passed by the learned Ist Addl. Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi, in awarding Rs.1,47,600/- to the appellant may kindly be modified to Rs.19,00,000/- and above along with interest at 12% from the date of petition till realization by allowing the appeal, in the interest of justice and equity."
2.
The occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 13.11.2008, the injuries sustained by the appellant, and the coverage of the offending vehicle under a valid insurance policy are not in dispute.
The Tribunal, by its Judgment and Award dated NC: 2026:KHC-K:2093-DB HC-KAR 04.10.2017, awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,47,540/-.
Contending that the said compensation is grossly inadequate, the appellant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
The age of the appellant at the time of the accident being 27 years is also not in dispute.

2 3.
Though the appellant had examined the treating doctor as PW.2, the doctor did not specifically quantify the percentage of permanent disability suffered by the appellant.
It appears that for this reason, the Tribunal did not assess disability and instead awarded only Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
4. A perusal of the evidence of PW.2 indicates that the doctor had treated the appellant with Foley's catheter in-situ following the road traffic accident.
The doctor has deposed that the appellant had sustained a spinal injury and was treated conservatively.
The appellant was advised urodynamic evaluation to rule out neurogenic bladder due to trauma.

5. The examination revealed underactive bladder with poor detrusor contractility, and the appellant was advised clean intermittent self-catheterisation, per NC: 2026:KHC-K:2093-DB HC-KAR urethral Foley's catheterisation, or suprapubic cystostomy.

6. The doctor has further stated that the appellant would have to remain on Foley's drainage throughout his life, with continuous monitoring of serum creatinine and urine examination every three to six months.
A serious warning was also expressed that if such medical care is not adhered to, the patient may develop renal failure.
The doctor also categorically stated that the appellant would not be able to have normal sexual activity.
7. PW.2 has been cross-examined, and the suggestions put to him have been denied.
Thus, the evidence of the doctor has remained unshaken.

8. The appellant has also produced various medical records including treatment records, laboratory reports, ultrasound reports, CT scan reports, discharge cards, prescriptions and X-ray films marked as Ex.P11 to Ex.P41.
9.
An application under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed before this Court seeking permission to produce additional evidence.

Considering the seriousness of NC: 2026:KHC-K:2093-DB HC-KAR the injuries sustained by the appellant, this Court permitted additional evidence to be recorded before the Additional Registrar General of this Court.

10. Pursuant thereto, the following documents were marked:
10.1.
Medical bills - Ex.P42 (series) 10.2.
Train tickets - Ex.P43 (series) 10.3.
Bus tickets - Ex.P44 (series) 10.4.
Discharge summary - Ex.P45 10.5.
Diagnostic reports - Ex.P46 (53 in number) 10.6.
Prescriptions - Ex.P47 10.7.
X-ray films - Ex.P48 11.
A perusal of Ex.P42 series indicate that these are medical bills relating to tests conducted at the Institute of Nephro-Urology, Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.

12. PW.2 has also deposed that the train and bus tickets produced at Ex.P43 and Ex.P44 relate to the travel undertaken by the appellant to Bengaluru for specialised Dhanaraj vs Satyajit And Anr on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157723618/
3 medical treatment.

The discharge NC: 2026:KHC-K:2093-DB HC-KAR summary indicates that the appellant had been catheterised, and that the serum creatinine levels, which had increased, were subsequently reduced following treatment.
Cystoscopy was also conducted.
13. The diagnostic reports further indicate abnormalities in urine analysis.

The ultrasound reports reveal dilatation of the collecting system of the kidneys, ureteric dilatation, thickening of the bladder wall with trabeculations and cystitis, along with bilateral back- pressure changes and post-void residue.

14. The medical records produced before the Tribunal as well as before this Court clearly demonstrate that the appellant has suffered serious and permanent damage to his urinary and neurological system.
In such circumstances, the award of Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities by the Tribunal is wholly inadequate.

15. At this stage, it is necessary to note that the assessment of permanent disability for the purpose of awarding compensation is not confined merely to the medical percentage of disability, what is required to be assessed is the functional disability, namely, the impact of the injury on the earning capacity of NC: 2026:KHC-K:2093-DB HC-KAR the injured person having regard to the nature of the profession carried on by him.
16. In the present case, the appellant was working as a driver, which necessarily requires continuous mobility and the ability to operate a vehicle for long periods.
The evidence of PW.2 establishes that the appellant has sustained a spinal injury resulting in neurogenic bladder requiring lifelong catheterisation.
17. Such a condition would make it practically impossible for the appellant to continue his profession as a driver.
However, it cannot be ruled out that the appellant may still be able to undertake some other form of work.

18. Considering the nature of the injury, the lifelong medical consequences, and the loss of ability to pursue his previous occupation, the functional disability of the appellant can reasonably be assessed at 75%.
19. Insofar as compensation towards pain and suffering is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.25,000/-.
Considering the spinal injury sustained, the prolonged treatment undergone and the permanent consequences of the injury, the said NC: 2026:KHC-K:2093-DB HC-KAR amount is wholly inadequate.

Accordingly, the compensation under the head of pain and suffering is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
20.
The appellant would have necessarily been incapacitated for a considerable period during treatment and recovery.

Taking into account the nature of the injuries sustained, a sum of Dhanaraj vs Satyajit And Anr on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157723618/
4 Rs.25,500/- (Rs.4,250  6 months) is awarded towards loss of income during laid-up period.
21. The notional income as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the year 2008 is Rs.4,250/- per month.

Applying the multiplier method: Loss of future income =
Rs.4,250  12  17  75% = Rs.6,50,250/-
22.

The multiplier 17 is applied having regard to the age of the appellant being 27 years, in terms of the principles laid down in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.
23.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.50,000/- under the head Loss of amenities.

The evidence on record indicates that the appellant has sustained a spinal injury resulting in neurogenic bladder requiring NC: 2026:KHC-K:2093-DB HC-KAR lifelong catheterisation and that he will not be able to lead a normal sexual life.
24. Loss of amenities extends beyond recreational deprivation and includes the loss of normal bodily functions, social life, and marital relations.
Considering the young age of the appellant (27 years) and the lifelong consequences of the injury, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is wholly inadequate.
25. Accordingly, the compensation towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life is enhanced to Rs.5,00,000/-.
26. In terms of Ex.P42, an additional amount of Rs.4,514/- has been incurred towards medical expenses and the same is directed to be paid.

27. The appellant has incurred expenses towards travel for medical treatment as follows:
27.1.

Train tickets - Rs.2,880/-
27.2.

Bus tickets - Rs.3,870/-
28.
The said amounts are also directed to be paid.
The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses.
Considering that the appellant is required to remain on lifelong catheter drainage with periodic medical tests every three to six months, the said amount is wholly inadequate.
Accordingly, a global sum of Rs.3,00,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses.

Accordingly, we pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is partly allowed.
ii. The judgment of the Tribunal in MVC No.419/2013 dated 04.10.2017 is hereby modified.
The appellant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.14,87,014/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
iii. Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company shall deposit with the Tribunal the said amount along with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
